repaired.name: Scenario
repaired.script:
triggered := false
if (triggered == true) {
    wait until(not ((#Ent_Motion).motionSensor_motion == true))
    triggered = false
}
wait until((#Ent_Motion).motionSensor_motion == true)
(#Ent_Light).light_moveToBrightness(100, 0)
delay(3 SEC)
(#Ent_Light).switch_off()
triggered = true

diagnosis.summary: The IR specifies a rising-edge wait (`wait(MotionSensor.Motion == true, edge rising)`). The candidate polls the condition at the start of the body (`if (motion == true)`). At t=100ms, motion became true, but the candidate's `if` guard evaluated to false because it only runs at the start of the iteration (t=0). The IR fires immediately upon the rising edge, while the candidate misses it. This matches Example A (repeating rising edge implemented as periodic polling).
diagnosis.change_summary: Replaced the periodic `if` guard with a blocking two-wait rearm pattern. The script now blocks until the rising edge occurs (`wait until(P)`), executes the body, then blocks until the condition drops (`wait until(not P)`) to re-arm for the next rising edge. This ensures the action fires exactly when the edge occurs, preserving the IR's rising-edge semantics.
